title: When the Regiment Wakes
premise: In 1913, Bram Okafor drives for suffragist Edith Marlowe and quietly reads the letters he delivers, keeping a private ledger of names, debts, and promises that protects the town's vulnerable. When the army requisitions the town for a training camp, it seizes the ledger too, and a colonel begins using its contents to blackmail and disappear anyone who resists. Bram must steal the ledger back, testify to what he knows before a government inquiry closes, and get the truth on record ahead of the victors' historians — succeeding at terrible cost, as Edith dies securing the evidence and Bram ends the century's turn as the town's reluctant keeper of memory.
about_author: Xanthe Reyes is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing requisition records from England's wartime training camps. She writes historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Other People's Letters
chapters.summary: Bram Okafor, driver and secret reader of his employer's correspondence, introduces the town of Ashden Vale and the ledger he keeps of names and silences. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: quiet pride in a dangerous competence, and the loneliness of knowing everyone's secrets while belonging to no one.

chapters.title: Miss Marlowe's War
chapters.summary: Edith Marlowe plans a suffrage rally; Bram ferries her past hostile crowds and sees how she weaponizes visibility while he weaponizes invisibility. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: wary mutual respect deepening into trust — the first belonging Bram has felt in years.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Army officers arrive with papers claiming the town green, the mill, and every public record for a training camp. The parish clerk surrenders the ledgers, including one that shouldn't exist. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: dread — the moment safety becomes paperwork.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Colonel Havelock summons townspeople for 'voluntary interviews' and quotes, verbatim, things only the ledger could contain. Bram realizes his private book is now state property. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: violation and guilt — his tool of protection turned instrument of power.

chapters.title: What Nell Buried
chapters.summary: Nell Ashcroft, whose illegitimate son is recorded in Bram's ledger, begs him to fix what he wrote. He can't. POV: Bram with a Nell interlude. Emotional beat: shame — the reader of letters learns words cannot be unread.

chapters.title: The First Disappearance
chapters.summary: A labor organizer who heckled Havelock vanishes overnight; the army calls it desertion after enlistment. Edith wants to protest publicly; Bram argues they'll need proof first. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the fracture between conscience and strategy.

chapters.title: Inside the Camp
chapters.summary: Bram takes a paid driving contract for the officers to see the camp from within: barbed wire around borrowed fields, soldiers bored and cruel, clerks filing names. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: cold clarity — he has walked into the archive of the enemy.

chapters.title: An Ally in Uniform
chapters.summary: Sergeant Pryce, a clerk ashamed of what he files, hints that the original ledger sits in the colonel's map room. Bram doesn't trust him but memorizes everything anyway. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: cautious hope, and the risk of hope.

chapters.title: The Rally They Allowed
chapters.summary: Edith holds her rally on the green now ringed by sentries; the speech becomes a eulogy for the missing man. Havelock watches from the steps, smiling. POV: alternating Bram/Edith. Emotional beat: defiance curdling into fear as the crowd disperses faster than ever before.

chapters.title: Blackmail by Ledger
chapters.summary: Havelock offers Bram a job: official driver, better pay, silence guaranteed — if Bram identifies which townspeople will cause trouble. He refuses without saying no. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: terror and resolve; the corruption of power shown as an invitation, not an order.

chapters.title: Nell's Choice
chapters.summary: Cornered by Havelock over her son, Nell agrees to inform on Edith in exchange for her boy's safety. She tells Bram herself, weeping. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: heartbreak — survival and betrayal wearing the same coat.

chapters.title: The Map Room
chapters.summary: Bram scouts the colonel's quarters during a dinner, counting locks, guards, and lamplight hours. He drafts a plan and shows no one. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: transformation — the invisible man begins to act.

chapters.title: What Edith Knew
chapters.summary: Edith reveals she suspected Bram read her letters all along, and that she has been feeding false secrets through him for a year. POV: Edith. Emotional bet: betrayal inverted into awe — their whole relationship re-seen, trust rebuilt on truth.

chapters.title: The Theft
chapters.summary: During a night exercise, Bram and Pryce lift the ledger from the map room; a sentry nearly catches them, and Pryce stays behind to cover the escape. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: breathless triumph shadowed by debt — someone paid for his courage.

chapters.title: Pryce's Fate
chapters.summary: Pryce is arrested for theft and will be court-martialed as a spy. Bram must decide whether rescue or testimony matters more. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: agonizing arithmetic of loyalty versus purpose.

chapters.title: The Inquiry Announced
chapters.summary: London sends a magistrate to investigate 'local disturbances' — clearly meant to whitewash. Edith resolves to testify; Havelock prepares his own tidy account. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: racing clock — the victors are already writing history.

chapters.title: Copies
chapters.summary: Bram and Edith spend three nights copying the ledger by hand, hiding pages in flour sacks and hymnals. Nell, unasked, copies the most damning section herself. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: communion — the town quietly conspiring toward truth.

chapters.title: The Raid on Marlowe House
chapters.summary: Soldiers search Edith's home for 'stolen military documents'; she burns decoy papers while the real copies sit in the church organ. She is arrested for obstruction. POV: Bram watching from across the street. Emotional beat: helpless fury — the cost of visibility.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: At the inquiry, Bram testifies, reading names aloud from memory even after the magistrate rules the ledger inadmissible. Havelock's cross-examination turns vicious; Bram does not flinch. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the climax — one invisible man making the record public, word by word.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: New Year's Eve 1913: the inquiry closes with a mild report, but Bram's testimony is printed in three newspapers, and London lawyers take up the disappeared man's case. Havelock is quietly reassigned, not punished. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: bitter victory — truth on record, justice deferred.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Edith is released; Pryce is sentenced but alive, and Bram arranges for his family to receive the truth in writing. Nell asks Bram to keep her son's name in the new ledger — this time openly. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: reconciliation — secrecy transformed into chosen stewardship.

chapters.title: When the Regiment Wakes
chapters.summary: Spring 1914: the regiment marches out, the town exhales, and Bram begins a second ledger — not of silences kept, but of truths witnessed, to be opened when the world is ready. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging; memory as the town's true inheritance.
